mainTopic: Witnesses undoing a שטר by claiming מודעא or אמנה, and a husband's חזקה in his wife's property
overview: This amud opens with the end of a קשיא. רב נחמן rules that witnesses who say 'it was a מודעא' are not believed, so how could the מודעא that רבה בר בר חנה signed cancel the sale שטר he also signed? The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's rule covers only an oral claim. A written מודעא is a document, and one document can weaken another. The גמרא then quotes רב נחמן's ruling in full, and מר בר רב אשי disagrees. He believes witnesses about a מודעא but not about אמנה, because a שטר with a מודעא may be written and an אמנה שטר may not. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that a husband has no חזקה on his wife's property, and asks why it is needed. It answers that the case is where he wrote 'I have no claim on your property.' When a ברייתא shows that such words mean nothing, דבי רבי ינאי answer that he wrote it while she was still an ארוסה, before his rights began. They support this with רב כהנא, whose words come on the next amud.

steps.title: Witnesses cannot cancel their own document by claiming it had a protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רב נחמן as a challenge. Witnesses who say 'our words were a מודעא' are not believed. So how could רבה בר בר חנה's מודעא cancel the sale שטר he signed?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Witnesses who say 'it was a trust document'] are not believed. 'Our words were a protest (מודעא)': they are not believed!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a challenge that started on the previous page. The גמרא uses רב נחמן's rule that witnesses cannot undo a שטר they signed by claiming there was a מודעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, רבה בר בר חנה signed a מודעא (a statement that the sale was forced) and also signed the sale שטר. If witnesses are never believed when they say 'there was a מודעא,' then his מודעא should not be able to cancel the sale שטר he himself signed.

keyTerms.meaning: A protest made ahead of time, declaring that a sale or gift about to happen is being done under pressure and is not truly willing
Believed; their claim is accepted
Our words, meaning the testimony we signed

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of a sentence. The first words, 'אין נאמנים,' finish רב נחמן's first case (אמנה), which appears on the previous page.

phrases.english: are not believed;
phrases.notes: This finishes רב נחמן's first case from the previous page: witnesses who say 'it was a trust document' are not believed.

phrases.english: 'Our words were accompanied by a protest'
they are not believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge against the case of רבה בר בר חנה from the previous page.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבה בר בר חנה's signed מודעא cancels the sale שטר he also signed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules that witnesses cannot undo a document they signed by saying there was a מודעא. That seems to contradict letting the מודעא cancel the sale.

steps.title: An oral claim cannot weaken a document, but another document can
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's rule applies only to an oral claim. A written מודעא is a document, and one document can weaken another.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies to a spoken claim, because spoken words cannot come and weaken a document. But with a document, one document can come and weaken another document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רב נחמן's rule. It covers only witnesses who speak up later. It does not cover a written מודעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words spoken later carry less weight than a written, signed שטר, so they cannot undo it. A written מודעא is equal in strength to the sale שטר, so it can weaken it. In רבה בר בר חנה's case the מודעא was written, so it works.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply to; this rule is limited to
Orally, by spoken words
A written document
Weakens, damages the strength of

steps.whatToRemember: An oral claim cannot undo a שטר. A written מודעא can.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule for the strength of documents: a written statement can challenge a written statement, but spoken words said afterward cannot.

phrases.english: That applies only to a spoken claim

phrases.aramaic: – דְּלָא אָתֵי עַל פֶּה וּמַרַע לִשְׁטָרָא,
phrases.english: because spoken words cannot come and weaken a document,
but with a document,
one document comes and weakens another document.
phrases.notes: Here the written מודעא is the document that weakens the sale document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by limiting רב נחמן's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited ruling (oral vs. written)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's rule seemed to block any מודעא from undoing a signed שטר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only oral claims. A written מודעא can weaken a written שטר.

steps.title: רב נחמן's full ruling on trust documents and protests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes רב נחמן's ruling in full. Witnesses who say 'it was a trust document' or 'it was a מודעא' are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב נחמן said: 'Our words were a trust arrangement': they are not believed. 'Our words were accompanied by a protest': they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word 'גופא,' the גמרא goes back to look directly at רב נחמן's statement that it quoted earlier. This sets up a disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treats both claims the same way. Once witnesses have signed a שטר, they cannot later say it was only an אמנה (a document given on trust before any loan happened) or that a מודעא went with it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier
Trust: a document written and handed over on trust before the loan or sale actually happened

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Nachman said:
'Our words were a trust arrangement': they are not believed,
'Our words were accompanied by a protest': they are not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the ruling quoted in step 1, now to examine it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are not believed to undo their signed שטר, whether they claim אמנה or מודעא.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי believes witnesses about a protest
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי agrees about אמנה but disagrees about מודעא. Witnesses who say there was a מודעא are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: 'Our words were a trust arrangement': they are not believed. 'Our words were accompanied by a protest': they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different ruling. He splits the two cases that רב נחמן treated the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that witnesses are not believed about אמנה. The disagreement is only about מודעא, which מר בר רב אשי accepts even from the witnesses' own mouths.

phrases.english: And Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
'Our words were a trust arrangement': they are not believed,
'Our words were accompanied by a protest': they are believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן's ruling in step 3 about מודעא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are not believed about אמנה, but they are believed about מודעא.

steps.title: Why a protest is different: it may be written, a trust document may not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains מר בר רב אשי's reason. A שטר with a מודעא is allowed to be written, but an אמנה שטר is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because this one may be written, and that one may not be written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why מר בר רב אשי treats the two claims differently, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing a sale שטר after a מודעא is allowed, because the seller is being forced. So witnesses who say they did it admit to nothing wrong. Writing an אמנה שטר is not allowed, so by the usual explanation, witnesses claiming it would be calling themselves wrongdoers, and they are not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Permitted to be written

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: no believing witnesses about either אמנה or מודעא. מר בר רב אשי: believe them about מודעא, because that שטר was allowed to be written, but not about אמנה, which was not.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'זה' (this one) means the מודעא case, and the second 'זה' (that one) means the אמנה case. This is the reverse of the order in מר בר רב אשי's ruling, which mentions אמנה first. In the reason, the case he believes (מודעא) comes first.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because this one may be written,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the document written with a מודעא.

phrases.english: and that one may not be written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind מר בר רב אשי's distinction in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why מר בר רב אשי splits between אמנה and מודעא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שטר with a מודעא may be written, but an אמנה שטר may not be written.

steps.title: Isn't the husband's rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a husband has no חזקה on his wife's property. It asks why this needs saying, since he is allowed to eat the פירות anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a husband cannot make a חזקה on his wife's property. Isn't that obvious? He has a right to the fruits, so when he eats them, he is just eating fruits, not claiming the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It then asks why the משנה even needs to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works because using land for years with no protest suggests you bought it. But a husband already has the right to eat the פירות of his wife's property. So his eating proves nothing about owning the land, and the rule seems too obvious to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof of ownership made by using land openly for a set time
His wife's property
It's obvious! Why say it?
The fruits or produce of land

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לָאִישׁ חֲזָקָה בְּנִכְסֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And a man has no presumption of ownership in his wife's property, etc.
It is obvious!
Since he has a right to the fruits,
it is fruits that he is eating!
phrases.notes: He means: his eating shows only that he is using his right to the produce, not that he owns the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the מודעא discussion in steps 1-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה to teach that a husband has no חזקה on his wife's property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A husband already has the right to the פירות, so his eating them can never look like a claim of ownership. The rule seems obvious.

steps.title: The case is where he gave up his rights in writing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the husband wrote to his wife: 'I have no claim on your property.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where he wrote to her: 'I have no legal claim or involvement in your property.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the משנה to a special case. The husband had written that he gives up his rights to her property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he gave up his right to the פירות, his later eating of them could look like he bought the land from her. The משנה teaches that even so, he still has no חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for this case
I have no legal claim or dealings (a way of giving up rights)
Your (feminine) property

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he wrote to her:
"I have no legal claim or dealings in your property."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he gave up his right to the פירות, his eating them would show he bought the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after such a waiver, the משנה teaches he has no חזקה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says such words mean nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: what does his writing even do? A ברייתא says that saying 'I have no claim on this field' has no legal effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he wrote that, so what? We learned in a ברייתא: if someone tells another person, 'I have no claim on this field,' or 'I have no dealings with it,' or 'My hands are removed from it,' he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 7. It shows from a ברייתא that these words of giving up rights do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If such a statement means nothing, then the husband's writing did not remove his right to the פירות. So he is back to the normal case, and the משנה is obvious again.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no dealings with it
My hands are removed
He has said nothing (it has no legal effect)

phrases.english: And if he wrote to her, what of it?
But it is taught: One who says to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: ״דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ״,
phrases.english: "I have no legal claim or dealings concerning this field,"
or "I have no business with it,"
or "My hands are removed from it" –
he has not said anything!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כְּתַב לַהּ – מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husband's written waiver changes anything.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that words like 'I have no claim on this field' have no legal effect, so the waiver should not remove his right to the פירות.

steps.title: He wrote it while she was still an ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי answer that the husband wrote the waiver while she was only an ארוסה, before his rights began. They support this with רב כהנא, whose words come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: The משנה is talking about a man who wrote this to her while she was still only engaged. And this follows רב כהנא, as רב כהנא said:
steps.whatsHappening: דבי רבי ינאי answer the challenge by setting the case at the time of אירוסין. The גמרא is setting up the next move: it is about to quote רב כהנא as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about giving up something a person already owns, which these words cannot do. Here the husband wrote while she was an ארוסה, before he had any right to her פירות, so he can stop those rights from ever starting. רב כהנא's statement, quoted next, backs this up.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (students) of רבי ינאי
A betrothed woman, before the marriage is completed
Our משנה
And this is like the view of רב כהנא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the husband can never give up rights. The point is timing: before marriage his rights to her property have not started yet.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said about it:
Our mishna is about one who writes to her
while she is still betrothed –
and this is in line with Rav Kahana,
as Rav Kahana said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: מַתְנִיתִין בְּכוֹתֵב לָהּ וְעוֹדָהּ אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא challenge from step 8 and begins bringing support from רב כהנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The waiver is meaningless, like the ברייתא's case of giving up a field.
steps.terutzMaskana: The waiver works because it was written while she was an ארוסה, before his rights to her property began.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that giving up a right can work if it is done before the right starts, even when it cannot work afterward.
